instrument_name: Florida Constitution Art. X s.24 Florida minimum wage
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum wage $10.00 from 2021-09-30, +$1.00 each 30 September until $15.00 on 2026-09-30 (so $14.00 2025-09-30 to 2026-09-29; $15.00 from 2026-09-30). From 30 Sep 2027 and each 30 Sep after, adjusted by CPI-W for 12 months to 1 Sep, published and effective the following 1 January (first indexed rate 2028-01-01). Tip credit capped at the FLSA tip credit allowable in 2003 ($3.02 = 5.15 - 2.13, derived): tipped cash wage $10.98 then $11.98 from 2026-09-30. Terms Employer/Employee/Wage per FLSA. (f) does not preempt higher wages adopted by other public bodies (but see 218.077 preemption). SOL 4 yrs / 5 yrs willful.

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 448.110 Florida Minimum Wage Act (2026 Statutes)
figure_or_rule_carried: Implements Art. X s.24; only FLSA-covered individuals entitled to state minimum wage; FLSA ss.13-14 exemptions incorporated. (4)(b) DOR and Department of Commerce post the adjusted rate by 15 October each year, notice mailed to registered employers by 15 November. Text still states $6.15 and the pre-2020 annual 1 January CPI-W South indexing: superseded in amount and schedule by the 2020 constitutional amendment (US-FLS5-001). Pre-suit 15-day written notice before a minimum-wage claim; liquidated damages; AG fine $1,000 per willful violation.

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 443.1217 Wages (reemployment tax taxable wage base, 2026 Statutes)
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wage base: remuneration in excess of the first $7,000 paid to an individual by an employer (or predecessor) in a calendar year is excluded, beginning 2015-01-01. Fixed in statute, not indexed. Confirms US-FL-004 (DOR page) on the 2026 statute edition.

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 443.131 Contributions (2026 Statutes)
figure_or_rule_carried: Contributions accrue per calendar quarter on wages paid; employer-only: an employer may not deduct contributions, interest, penalties, fines or fees from employee wages (443.131(1)). Rounding: fraction under half a cent disregarded, half a cent or more raised to 1 cent. Initial rate 2.7% while chargeable for fewer than 8 calendar quarters; standard rate 5.4%; variation from standard only when chargeable throughout 12 consecutive quarters ending 30 June of the preceding year; computed rate not rounded below 0.1%; maximum assigned rate 5.4% (+1 point for short-time-compensation employers charged). Domestic-only employers eligible for variation may elect annual reporting/payment, due 31 January, application by 1 December of the prior year.

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 443.1216 Employment (coverage and exemptions, 2026 Statutes)
figure_or_rule_carried: UI coverage: corporate officers and common-law employees covered (1)(a); employee-leasing workers reported under the leasing company's account. Public employers covered (2) except elected officials, legislators/judiciary, temporary emergency staff, major nontenured policymaking positions. Nonprofit 3306(c)(8) organisations covered with 4+ workers in 20 weeks (3). Agricultural labor covered if $10,000 cash wages in a quarter or 5+ workers in 20 weeks (5). Domestic service covered if $1,000 cash in a quarter (6). Localization (7) as US-MULTI-001. Exempt (13): church/religious-order employment and ministers, family employment (by son/daughter/spouse; child under 21 by parent), students employed by their school, student nurses/interns, commission-only insurance agents and real-estate salespersons, newspaper delivery under 18, foreign government, election workers under $1,000.

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 443.163 Electronic reporting and remitting of contributions (2026 Statutes)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer with 10 or more employees in any quarter of the preceding state fiscal year must file the Employer's Quarterly Report (incl. corrections) and remit contributions electronically. Penalty for a non-electronic report: $25 per report + $1 per employee, max $300; $25 per non-electronic remittance. Waiver by the tax collection service provider (DOR).

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 443.151(1) Posting of information (reemployment assistance)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer must post benefit-rights statements prescribed by FloridaCommerce rule and supply claim materials to individuals as directed by rule (any separation-notice form is fixed by rule, not by statute; the rule was not read).

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 409.2576 State Directory of New Hires (2026 Statutes)
figure_or_rule_carried: Administered by DOR. Every new or rehired employee reported within 20 days of hire date (date of hire = first day of work for which income is owed), or by two monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart if electronic; W-4 or equivalent; fields: employee name, address, date of hire, SSN; employer name, address, FEIN; DOB optional. Multistate electronic reporters may designate one state (notify HHS). Service recipients must also report non-employees paid $600+ per calendar year within 20 days (name, address, SSN/TIN, date services first rendered, recipient name/address/EIN).

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 218.077 Wage and employment benefits requirements by political subdivisions (preemption)
figure_or_rule_carried: Counties, municipalities and other political subdivisions may not mandate a minimum wage other than state/federal, nor employment benefits (incl. paid/unpaid sick leave, vacation, holidays) not required by state/federal law, nor control contractor wages through purchasing (ch. 2024-80). Exceptions: their own employees; employers receiving a direct tax abatement/subsidy as a condition. Ch. 2024-80 amendments do not impair contracts entered before 2026-09-30. Result: no local minimum wage or local paid-sick-leave mandate on private employers in Florida.

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 448.095 Employment eligibility (E-Verify)
figure_or_rule_carried: Verify each new employee within 3 business days of the first day working for pay; public agencies and private employers with 25+ employees must use E-Verify (from 2023-07-01); each E-Verify employer certifies compliance on its first reemployment tax return each calendar year (a field on the first RT-6 of the year).

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 450.081 Hours of work of minors
figure_or_rule_carried: Minors 15 and under: not before 7am/after 7pm on school nights, max 15 h/week in school session, 3 h on school days; holidays/summer 7am-9pm, 8 h/day, 40 h/week; max 6 consecutive days; 30-min meal after 4 h. Minors 16-17: not before 6:30am/after 11pm on school nights, 8 h on school-night days, 30 h/week in session (waivable by parent or superintendent); 30-min meal after 4 h when working 8+ h. Exemptions: graduates, certificate holders, hardship, home/virtual education 16-17, domestic service in private homes, children of the employer. No minor sub-minimum wage in state law.

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 222.11 Exemption of wages from garnishment
figure_or_rule_carried: Head of family (provides more than half the support of a child/dependent): all disposable earnings exempt if disposable earnings <= $750/week; above $750/week not garnishable unless the employee waived in writing (separate 14-point form), and then capped at CCPA 15 U.S.C. 1673. Others: CCPA limit. Exempt earnings stay exempt 6 months in a bank account if traceable. Not indexed.

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 61.1301 Income deduction orders (child support)
figure_or_rule_carried: Payor may charge the obligor up to $5 for the first deduction and $2 per deduction thereafter (within the CCPA 1673(b) limit incl. charges); implement no later than the first payment date more than 14 days after service; remit within 2 days after each pay date; arrears add 20% or more of the periodic amount; income deduction has priority over all other legal processes under state law; multiple orders prorated with priority to current support; termination notice to obligee/IV-D agency (civil penalty $250 first / $500 subsequent); no discharge for income deduction.

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 741.313 Domestic/sexual violence leave
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers with 50+ employees, employee with 3+ months service: up to 3 working days in any 12 months, paid or unpaid at employer discretion; employee must first exhaust annual/vacation, personal and sick leave unless waived; confidentiality.

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 40.271 Jury service (employment protection)
figure_or_rule_carried: No dismissal for jury service; the section sets no duty for a private employer to pay wages during jury service.

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 448.08 Attorney's fees in actions for unpaid wages
figure_or_rule_carried: Court may award costs and a reasonable attorney's fee to the prevailing party in an action for unpaid wages. Only general wage-recovery provision; ch.448 has no final-pay timing or vacation-payout rule (section list US-FL-P5-2-004).

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 501.171 Security of confidential personal information
figure_or_rule_carried: Personal information includes name + SSN, ID numbers, financial account numbers; covered entities must take reasonable measures to protect it; breach notice to the Department of Legal Affairs if 500+ Floridians affected within 30 days (+15 for good cause); individual notice; secure disposal (shred/erase) of records when no longer retained. No Florida statute on SSN truncation on pay statements located.

instrument_name: Florida DOR Reemployment Tax Rate Information page (2026 rates)
figure_or_rule_carried: Initial rate 0.0270 (2.7%) until the employer has reported for 10 quarters; experience rate thereafter (benefits charged / taxable payroll, first seven of the last nine quarters). 2026: minimum 0.0010 (0.1%) = $7 per employee, maximum 0.0540 (5.4%) = $378 per employee, on wages up to $7,000. Rate notice RT-20 mailed yearly; protest within 20 days. Same figures as US-FL-004, now with a local copy (curl 2026-11-02). Derivation: 7000 x 0.001 = 7; 7000 x 0.054 = 378.

instrument_name: Florida DOR Florida Reemployment Tax overview page (incl. E-Verify certification)
figure_or_rule_carried: Reemployment tax paid by employers only; first $7,000 per employee per calendar year taxable; DOR registers employers, collects reports, assigns rates and audits since 2000; FloridaCommerce administers benefits. E-Verify: employers with 25+ employees, public agencies and ELCs certify on the first reemployment tax return of each calendar year (or Form RT-E Verify); certification valid one calendar year, signed by owner/officer/partner.

instrument_name: Florida DOR Employer Guide to Reemployment Tax (RT-800002, R. 03/25)
article_or_section: pp.2-3 liability; pp.8-11 RT-6, wage base, annual option, taxable/exempt wages, BLS-3020, RT-6EW, E-Verify
figure_or_rule_carried: Liability: $1,500 wages in a quarter, or 1 employee in 20 weeks, or FUTA liability (current/preceding year); domestic $1,000 in a quarter. RT-6 due by the last day of the month after the quarter (Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31); report required even with no tax due; electronic payment initiated by 5 pm ET the business day before the due date. RT-7 annual domestic report due Jan 1, late after Jan 31. Wage portion: name, SSN, gross and taxable wages per employee; penalty up to $300 for wrong/missing SSN. Wages reported when paid. $7,000 base per employer; successor may count predecessor wages; out-of-state wages credited via RT-6NF. Taxable: commissions (except solely-commissioned real estate/insurance agents and barbers), bonuses, back pay, tips reported under IRC 6053(a), non-cash remuneration, personal-use car, non-convenience meals/lodging, group legal, golden parachutes. Exempt: church/minister, students at their school, co-op students, family employment, cafeteria plan payments not reportable to IRS, IRC 127 education. Multi-worksite employers file BLS-3020 quarterly; contractors to public/nonprofit educational institutions file RT-6EW.

instrument_name: Florida DOR Employer's Quarterly Report RT-6 (R. 07/23) and instructions RT-6N (R. 07/23), Rule 73B-10.037 F.A.C.
figure_or_rule_carried: RT-6 covers one calendar quarter; Line 1 covered employees in the pay period including the 12th of each month; Line 2 gross wages (incl. vacation/sick pay, bonuses, back pay, non-cash; tips when used for minimum wage or reported at $20+/month; excluding 443.1217(2)(b)-(g) items); Line 3 excess wages over $7,000 (incl. wages reported to another state, predecessor wages); Line 4 taxable = 2 - 3; Line 5 tax = Line 4 x rate. Due last day of month after quarter (next business day if weekend/holiday); electronic filing and payment mandatory for employers with 10+ employees in any quarter of the prior state fiscal year (Jul-Jun). Prior-quarter corrections on RT-8A (online if e-filer). Signed by owner/officer/partner or authorised agent. Form on Rule 73B-10.037 F.A.C. (rule text not read).

instrument_name: Florida DOR Reemployment Tax Import File Specifications for Flat File Web Import, Version 7 (December 2023)
figure_or_rule_carried: Fixed-length text import of RT-6 and RT-8A to the DOR File and Pay application: five record types 00 Header (FEIN, RT account number), 01 Employer (name, address, filing quarter with leading zero, totals, contact), 02 Employee (SSN, name, wages; optional for RT-6, required for RT-8A), 03 Total (monthly covered employee counts), 99 Trailer (submission date YYYYMMDD). Currency fields with two implied decimals; numeric fields zero-padded; special characters barred; zip files not accepted. 8,000+ records: file in first two weeks of the due month; more than 20,000 employee records: XML upload required. Resolves the open RT-6 layout gap of US-FIL-015.

instrument_name: Florida DOR Reemployment Tax XML Package FL_RT_XML_Schemas_v2026 1.0 (flRtXmlPkg.zip)
authority: Florida Department of Revenue (Software Developer Information and Specifications)
article_or_section: 9 XSD (RT_FLTransmission, FLReturnDataState, FLReturnHeaderState, FLStatePayment, FLStateUI, efileTypes, efileStateTypes, efileMessageState, FLefileMessage); RT_XML_Guide_v2026_1.0.pdf; RT_XPath_v2026_1.0.xlsx; samples RT-6/RT-8A/manifests; 4 test cases; RT_changes.xlsx
figure_or_rule_carried: XML channel for RT-6 and RT-8A (IRS efile Transmission namespace http://www.irs.gov/efile); required above 20,000 employee records. FLReturnHeaderState carries an optional E-Verify certification block (Name, Title...). Archive extracted 2026-11-02 (20 files); the RT-6 Sample.xml validates against RT_FLTransmission.xsd with lxml (True; the 'State Schemas' folder renamed without the space so lxml can resolve includes). Developers file Form DR-600001; contact e-vendor@floridarevenue.com. Archive retained, not expanded in the corpus.

instrument_name: Florida DOR Reemployment Tax Report and Payment Information page
figure_or_rule_carried: Channels: direct entry, text-file import, XML upload (required above 20,000 employee records). Paper RT-6 mailed to non-mandatory filers; voluntary e-filing for 2 consecutive quarters stops paper forms. Report lists total, excess and taxable wages, tax due and each employee's name, SSN and total wages; ITIN (starts with 9) is not a substitute for an SSN; SSN validity rules (no 000/666, middle 00, last 0000). Penalty for erroneous/incomplete report: greater of $50 or 10% of tax due, max $300 per report, waivable once in 12 months if corrected within 30 days. Only own payroll unless ELC or approved common paymaster; payrolling not authorised.

instrument_name: Florida DOR Wages Paid to Alien Workers page
figure_or_rule_carried: Wages of non-U.S. citizens in Florida are subject to reemployment tax like citizens' wages; the exemption in 443.1216(13)(v) covers nonresident aliens temporarily present as F or J nonimmigrants performing services for the F/J purpose (page names two exemptions in total; second exemption in the page tail, not transcribed).

instrument_name: Florida DOR poster RT-83 'To Employees' (R. 10/26)
figure_or_rule_carried: Mandatory reemployment-assistance poster (443.151(1)): employer registered with DOR; reemployment taxes are paid by the employer and by law cannot be deducted from wages; claims at connect.myflorida.com. Revision R. 10/26 is current (supersedes earlier editions).

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 448.01 Legal day's work; extra pay
figure_or_rule_carried: For persons employed to perform manual labor by the day/week/month/year, 10 hours is a legal day's work unless a written contract signed by both sets fewer or more hours; without such contract, extra pay is due for work required beyond 10 hours a day. No premium rate is fixed (the 1.5x weekly overtime comes only from FLSA). Florida has no other daily or weekly overtime statute.
